editorial:
Imagine you are hanging out with your friends in San Francisco when you stumble upon something totally gross and scary. You find a nest of bloodthirsty monsters hiding right inside the tower of the Golden Gate Bridge. It is a wild setup that feels like those classic eighties movies where teenagers get into way too much trouble. The vibe is all about that neon-soaked city look mixed with some old-school monster scares. You will feel for the kids because they try to do the right thing and warn the adults, but since the monsters are so well hidden, the police just think they are playing pranks. It creates a lot of tension because you know the danger is real while the grown-ups are just shaking their heads.

What really works here are the creature effects and the fast movement of the plot. While some of the acting is a bit over the top, it fits the cheesy style of the era perfectly. The best part is seeing how the group uses their wits to survive when no one will help them. If you enjoy campy horror, you should definitely check this out. You can grab a 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection for the best picture quality, or just look for it to rent on Apple TV for a quick movie night with friends.
endingExplained: In the final showdown, the teens lure the monsters out of the bridge tower using a loud noise trap. They manage to blow up the nest using stolen explosives, which kills most of the creatures in a big fire. Just when you think they are safe, one monster survives and attacks the lead guy, but his friends save him at the last second. They finally get the evidence they need to prove the monsters existed.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves 80s creature features and teen adventure movies.
